subject: Maths
title: Parallel and perpendicular lines
subtitle: Straight-Line Graphs · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can identify and find equations of parallel and perpendicular lines.

key_vocab.definition: Parallel lines have the same gradient (m₁ = m₂). Perpendicular lines have gradients that multiply to give -1.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can identify and find equations of parallel and perpendicular lines.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: Parallel lines -- Parallel lines have the same gradient (m₁ = m₂). Perpendicular lines have gradients that multiply to give -1.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Parallel: same gradient. Perpendicular: gradients multiply to -1.
m₁ × m₂ = -1 ⇒ m₂ = -&frac{1}{m₁}
Negative reciprocal for perpendicular lines

Key examples:
  ✓ y = 2x + 1 and y = 2x - 3 are parallel  (same gradient m = 2)
  ✓ y = 3x and y = -&frac{1}{3}x are perpendicular  (3 × -&frac{1}{3} = -1)
  ✓ Negative reciprocal of 4 is -&frac{1}{4}  (flip and negate)
  ✗ y = 2x + 1 and y = -2x + 3 are parallel  (gradients are 2 and -2, not equal)
  ✗ Perpendicular to gradient 3 is &frac{1}{3}  (must be -&frac{1}{3})

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – identifying parallel lines
  Are y = 3x + 5 and y = 3x - 2 parallel?
  Gradient of first line = 3
  Gradient of second line = 3
  Same gradient, so they are parallel
  Yes, parallel
  (Parallel lines have equal gradients but different y-intercepts.)

Example 2 – perpendicular gradient
  Find the gradient perpendicular to y = 4x + 1.
  Original gradient m = 4
  Negative reciprocal: -&frac{1}{4}
  Perpendicular gradient = -&frac{1}{4}
  m = -&frac{1}{4}
  (Flip the fraction and change the sign.)

sections.title: Identifying parallel lines
sections.content:
State whether each pair is parallel, perpendicular, or neither.

(a) y = 5x + 1 and y = 5x - 4
(b) y = 2x and y = -&frac{1}{2}x + 3
(c) y = 3x + 2 and y = -3x + 2
(d) y = x + 7 and y = -x + 1

sections.title: Negative reciprocals
Equations of parallel lines
sections.content:
Find the equation of the parallel line through the given point.

(a) Parallel to y = 4x + 1 through (2, 11)
(b) Parallel to y = -x + 5 through (3, 1)
(c) Parallel to y = &frac{1}{2}x - 3 through (4, 0)
(d) Parallel to y = 3x through (1, 7)

sections.title: Equations of perpendicular lines
sections.content:
Find the equation of the perpendicular line through the given point.

(a) Perpendicular to y = 2x + 5 through (4, 1)
(b) Perpendicular to y = -3x + 2 through (3, 5)
(c) Perpendicular to y = &frac{1}{4}x through (8, 0)
(d) Perpendicular to y = -x + 6 through (1, 3)

sections.title: Mixed problems
sections.content:
Solve each problem.

(a) Line through (2, 5) parallel to y = 3x - 1. Equation?
(b) Line perpendicular to y = 5x at (0, 2). Equation?
(c) Are 2x + y = 4 and y = -2x + 7 parallel?
(d) Gradient of line perpendicular to 4x + 2y = 6?
(e) Perpendicular to y = &frac{2}{3}x + 1 through (4, -1). Equation?

teacher_sections.title: Teacher Key & Mark Scheme
teacher_sections.content:
Award marks for correct working and final answers.

Identifying parallel lines:
  (a) Parallel
  (b) Perpendicular
  (c) Neither
  (d) Perpendicular

Negative reciprocals:
  (a) m = -&frac{1}{2}
  (b) m = &frac{1}{5}
  (c) m = -&frac{4}{3}
  (d) m = 3

Equations of parallel lines:
  (a) y = 4x + 3
  (b) y = -x + 4
  (c) y = &frac{1}{2}x - 2
  (d) y = 3x + 4

Equations of perpendicular lines:
  (a) y = -&frac{1}{2}x + 3
  (b) y = &frac{1}{3}x + 4
  (c) y = -4x + 32
  (d) y = x + 2

Mixed problems:
  (a) y = 3x - 1
  (b) y = -&frac{1}{5}x + 2
  (c) Yes (both m = -2)
  (d) m = &frac{1}{2}
  (e) y = -&frac{3}{2}x + 5
